elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph: "TrueLink shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty running to Client and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "shall defend and indemnify Client and its affiliates against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of..." covers third-party claims for Client and affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "an allegation that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the agreement's own service/deliverable nomenclature.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data caused by TrueLink" — covers all Client data, not selected types.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (iv): "TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Client shall promptly notify TrueLink of any such claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "Client shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Rendered 12(a)(i) still reads "any claim arising out of or relating to the Web Site or Client Content or other content provided by Client". The retained "arising out of or relating to the Web Site" hook is broader than Customer-provided content — it captures any claim connected with Client's site (including conduct, transactions and third-party product/service claims previously in the deleted prong (iv)), so the Client indemnity is not limited to Client-provided content plus Client's breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i) gives a TrueLink defence/indemnity for third-party allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate IP.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no modification exclusion is required and none is added, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is imposed, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion is imposed, so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no procure/modify/replace remedy obligation; nothing elsewhere in the rendered text supplies one.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy appears in the inserted or retained language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual fees super-cap is drafted; the comment expressly declines to add one.

reasons: Nine of ten preferred elements are met by the inserted TrueLink defence/indemnity paragraph (IP infringement, breach of law, TrueLink-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice, control and cooperation), and the favourable existing 12(b) breach indemnity is retained.

Preferred level is incomplete on the Customer-indemnity narrowing: rendered 12(a)(i) retains "arising out of or relating to the Web Site or". Repair by deleting "the Web Site or" so the prong reads "any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content or other content provided by Client", leaving only content-based and Client-law-violation prongs.

Fallback level is not reached either: no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund of applicable fees where those remedies are unavailable, and no 3× annual fees super-cap. Because neither checklist is complete, the redline is not position-complete as drafted.

Minimality holds: the edits touch only the two targeted provisions, add no survival tail, expense, damages-category or procedural boilerplate beyond the notice/control/cooperation mechanic the preferred checklist requires, and the deletions in 12(a) (breach-of-Agreement, System/Credit Repository default and product-injury prongs) are exactly what the narrowing element requires. Recommended trim only: "or other content provided by Client" is largely redundant of the defined "Client Content" and needlessly widens our own indemnity.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is left dangling, the retained TrueLink breach indemnity is not contradicted by the new paragraph, and the inserted limbs use the agreement's own service and Client Content nomenclature.
